title: Strictly perfect affine cone models
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an affine open, and $T$ a distinguished triangle of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Suppose strictly perfect complexes $A^\bullet,B^\bullet$ [def-pc-perfect-complex] represent $T_1|_U,T_2|_U$. Then there is a strictly perfect complex $K^\bullet$ representing $T_3|_U$.

proof.text: Exact open restriction [lem-sc-derived-hom-mayer-vietoris] carries $T$ to a distinguished triangle. Conjugate its first arrow by the given representing isomorphisms, and apply [lem-pc-perfect-affine-map-representative] to get a chain map $\alpha:A\to B$ whose localized arrow is that conjugated arrow.

Construct $K=C(\alpha)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its degree $i$ term is $A^{i+1}\oplus B^i$. If the bounds of $A,B$ are $[a_1,b_1],[a_2,b_2]$, this is zero outside $[\min(a_1-1,a_2),\max(b_1-1,b_2)]$. The biproduct of their finite-free retract pairs is again a retract pair, by checking the two projections. A binary sum of finite free sheaves is free on the disjoint union of their finite bases; reindex by a finite ordinal and its universe lift. Thus $K$ satisfies precisely [def-pc-perfect-complex], including zero-rank retracts.

The image of the cone triangle under $Q$ is distinguished [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its first arrow agrees with the restricted arrow by the representative equation. TR3 [def-weil-triangulated-category] completes the first two isomorphisms to a triangle morphism; [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the third component an isomorphism. Its inverse gives $T_3|_U\cong Q(K)$.
